p.text: What has Kamola learned this year?
options: How much a single word can cost

fb.correct: 'It was not until this year that I understood how much one word costs.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'It was not until this year that I understood how much one word costs.'

1.say: All I want is a straight answer about the funding. You will not get one today. The reason why I keep asking is that I have to tell forty parents something. Then tell them what is certain and label the rest as uncertain. That is exactly what I object to. It sounds evasive. It is precise, not evasive. There is a distinction. Not to a parent at eight in the morning. Look at the wording. 'We have only applied' and 'we have applied only for the building' are different claims. So where do I put the word? Next to the part you mean to limit. Put it anywhere else and you have said something you did not mean. It was not until this year that I understood how much one word costs. That is the whole job, most weeks.

key: It is precise, not evasive. There is a distinction.

grammar.label: cleft variations — All I want, The reason why, It was not until
grammar.form: All/The only thing + (that) + clause + is; The reason why … is that; It was not until … that
grammar.meaning: focuses one element and backgrounds the rest

explanation.en: Beyond 'What I need is…', B2 English uses 'All I want is an answer', 'The reason why it failed is that nobody checked', and 'It was not until Friday that we heard'. Each puts one element under the spotlight.
explanation.uz: 'What I need is…' dan tashqari B2 darajasida 'All I want is an answer', 'The reason why it failed is that nobody checked', 'It was not until Friday that we heard' qurilmalari ishlatiladi. Har biri bitta bo'lakni ajratib ko'rsatadi.

grammar.positive_example: It was not until the second reading that anyone noticed the error.
grammar.negative_example: It was not until the second reading when anyone noticed the error.

l1_notes.uz: 'The reason why … is because' takroriy sabab bildiradi; to'g'ri shakli 'is that'.

grammar.label: focus adverbs and their position — only, even, just, particularly
grammar.form: adverb placed immediately before the element it focuses
grammar.meaning: the position of the adverb changes which element is limited or emphasised

explanation.en: 'Only' and 'even' attach to whatever follows them. 'I only asked for the report' (I did nothing more) is not 'I asked only for the report' (nothing else). In careful writing, put the focus adverb next to the element it belongs to.
explanation.uz: 'Only' va 'even' o'zidan keyingi bo'lakka tegishli bo'ladi. 'I only asked for the report' va 'I asked only for the report' — ma'nolari har xil. Aniq yozishda fokus ravishi tegishli bo'lagi yoniga qo'yiladi.

grammar.positive_example: She reads only the first page, never the rest.
grammar.negative_example: She only reads the first page, never the rest.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida 'faqat' va 'hatto' odatda so'zdan oldin turadi, shuning uchun ingliz tilidagi joylashuv qoidasi tanish — lekin so'zlashuvda ingliz tili ko'pincha fe'l oldiga qo'yadi, yozma tilda esa yo'q.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: All I want is a straight answer about the funding.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You will not get one today.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The reason why I keep asking is that I have to tell forty parents something.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then tell them what is certain and label the rest as uncertain.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is exactly what I object to. It sounds evasive.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: It is precise, not evasive. There is a distinction.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Not to a parent at eight in the morning.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Look at the wording. 'We have only applied' and 'we have applied only for the building' are different claims.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: So where do I put the word?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Next to the part you mean to limit. Put it anywhere else and you have said something you did not mean.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It was not until this year that I understood how much one word costs.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is the whole job, most weeks.
